name: gen8_ppgtt_create
prose: Returns struct i915_ppgtt * or an ERR_PTR (gen8_ppgtt.c:1002-1085). It allocates the ppgtt with kzalloc and returns ERR_PTR(-ENOMEM) if that fails. Otherwise it calls ppgtt_init, sets vm.top to 3 for a 4-level vm and 2 otherwise, sets pd_shift, sets has_read_only to false for graphics versions 11 and 12 and true otherwise, selects alloc_pt_dma (LMEM or system variant by HAS_LMEM), alloc_scratch_dma, pte_encode (gen12 or gen8 variant), bind_async_flags, insert_entries, insert_page, allocate_va_range, clear_range, foreach and cleanup. It then initialises the scratch page (gen8_init_scratch), allocates the top-level page directory (gen8_alloc_top_pd), preallocates the top-level PDPs when the vm is not 4-level, notifies the vGPU layer when a vGPU is active, and calls gen8_init_rsvd. A failure of any of those steps (scratch, top pd, preallocation or gen8_init_rsvd) goes to err_put, which releases the vm with i915_vm_put and returns ERR_PTR of that step's error. On success it returns the ppgtt, and the caller holds the one vm reference that it must release with i915_vm_put.
note: slice cut the head (function begins at gen8_ppgtt.c:1002). Reviewer claim (failure list omits the gen8_init_rsvd error path, which also returns ERR_PTR(err) after i915_vm_put) is right (1076-1078, 1082-1084). R:right

name: signal_irq_work
prose: Static void irq_work callback (intel_breadcrumbs.c:170-273) for a struct intel_breadcrumbs b; it returns nothing. It takes a timestamp and drains b->signaled_requests into a local list with llist_del_all if that list is non-empty. If that local list is empty, the irq is armed and b->signalers is empty, it disarms the interrupt. Then, under RCU and with b->signaler_active incremented, it walks every context in b->signalers and, for each context, its signals list: it stops at the first request that is not complete or whose I915_FENCE_FLAG_SIGNAL bit was not set (the bit is cleared with test_and_clear_bit). For each request taken, under ce->signal_lock it removes it from ce->signals and calls remove_signaling_context; if that releases the context from b->signalers it calls add_retire when the request is the timeline's last, and drops a context reference. It then signals the dma-fence: if __dma_fence_signal reports it was newly signaled the request is added to the local list, otherwise a request reference is dropped. After decrementing signaler_active and leaving RCU, each request on the local list gets its engine's retire_inflight_request_prio hook called if set, then under rq->lock its fence callbacks are moved to a local list, the fence timestamp is set and the callbacks are notified, and the request reference is dropped. Finally it arms the irq if it is not armed and signalers exist, and disarms it if it is armed and b->active is zero. New entries can be added to b->signaled_requests concurrently, so the list is not guaranteed to be empty at return.
note: Checked against intel_breadcrumbs.c:170-273. Reviewer claims: disarm needs no pending signals and no signalers (right, 206), entries drained from the llist are not removed from the context lists here (right, the context lists are handled by the rcu walk), and signaled_requests is not guaranteed empty afterwards (right, concurrent llist_add). R:right

name: heartbeat
prose: Static void work function (intel_engine_heartbeat.c:136-240). It flushes the engine's submission, takes engine->heartbeat.systole with xchg, drops that request if it already completed and puts it back otherwise. It then calls intel_engine_pm_get_if_awake and returns at once, leaving any pending systole, when the engine is not awake. With the wakeref held: if the GT is wedged it goes to out; if the scheduler engine is disabled it calls reset_engine with the systole and goes to out; if a systole request is still pending then, unless the current time is after the request's emitted_jiffies plus the heartbeat interval (so also when exactly equal), it goes to out; otherwise, if the request's submit fence has not signalled it does nothing, else if the engine can schedule and the request's priority is below I915_PRIORITY_BARRIER it raises its priority one step (normal, then heartbeat, then barrier), else it resets the engine; then it updates the request's emitted_jiffies and goes to out. With no pending systole it compares engine->serial with wakeref_serial and goes to out if equal; tries mutex_trylock on the kernel timeline (on failure, if the engine was already marked blocked for this serial it calls intel_gt_handle_error, then goes to out); otherwise it creates and commits a new heartbeat request (if creation fails it just unlocks). At out, if hangcheck is disabled or next_heartbeat says no more beats are needed, it drops any systole request; in all paths that took the wakeref it calls intel_engine_pm_put.
note: Checked against intel_engine_heartbeat.c:136-240. Reviewer claims: a stuck systole is not always escalated or reset (right: the not-yet-submitted case does neither, 175-185); the wedged path still drops the systole at out when hangcheck is disabled or next_heartbeat is false (right, 159-160 and 234-238); the delay test also exits when elapsed equals the interval (right, !time_after at 171). R:right

name: intel_gt_resume
prose: Returns int (intel_gt_pm.c:240-311). It first returns the error of intel_gt_has_unrecoverable_error(gt) if nonzero, before anything else. It then calls gt_sanitize(gt, true), takes a GT PM wakeref and FORCEWAKE_ALL forcewake, and sanitises rc6. If the GT is wedged it sets err to -EIO and goes to out_fw. It calls intel_gt_init_hw (on failure it logs and goes to err_wedged), finishes the uc reset, enables rps and llc, and for each engine takes an engine pm reference, increments engine->serial, calls intel_engine_resume and drops the reference; a failure of intel_engine_resume logs and goes to err_wedged. On success it enables rc6, resumes uc, drops the user forcewake and falls into out_fw. err_wedged calls intel_gt_set_wedged and goes to out_fw. At out_fw it releases the forcewake, the GT wakeref, marks the GT bind context ready and returns err, which is 0 on success, -EIO for the wedged case, or the error from intel_gt_init_hw or intel_engine_resume.
note: slice cut the head (function begins at intel_gt_pm.c:240). Reviewer claim (round 15: no early unrecoverable-error check exists and the wakeref is taken first) is wrong: the check is at 247-249, before gt_sanitize and intel_gt_pm_get. R:wrong

name: intel_ring_begin
prose: Returns u32 * (intel_ring.c:230-309): a pointer into the ring buffer where num_dwords u32 values can be written, or ERR_PTR(error). It requires (GEM_BUG_ON checks) an even num_dwords and bytes plus rq->reserved_space not above ring->effective_size. If the request plus reserved space does not fit before the end of the usable ring it either plans to wrap (when the request itself does not fit, need_wrap is the remaining tail size) or only counts the reserved space from the start. If the needed bytes exceed ring->space it calls wait_for_space and returns ERR_PTR of its nonzero result (ring->emit is not advanced, though ring->space may change while waiting). When wrapping, it fills the tail with MI_NOOP (zeros), subtracts the tail size from ring->space and sets ring->emit to 0. It then takes the pointer at ring->emit (poisoning the area when CONFIG_DRM_I915_DEBUG_GEM is enabled), advances ring->emit by num_dwords * 4 and decreases ring->space by the same amount, and returns the pointer.
note: slice cut the head (function begins at intel_ring.c:230). Reviewer claim (wrapping also subtracts need_wrap from ring->space, so total space decrease is more than the bytes) is right (296). R:right

name: xehp_sseu_info_init
prose: Static void (intel_sseu.c:208-250). It sets num_geometry_regs and num_compute_regs to 1 and calls intel_sseu_set_info(sseu, 1, 32 * max(1, 1), 8 or 16) where the EUs per subslice is 8 when HAS_ONE_EU_PER_FUSE_BIT is true and 16 otherwise; sets has_xehp_dss to 1; loads geometry_subslice_mask from GEN12_GT_GEOMETRY_DSS_ENABLE and compute_subslice_mask from GEN12_GT_COMPUTE_DSS_ENABLE only (xehp_load_dss_mask reads numregs registers, here 1, so the extra XEHPC_GT_COMPUTE_DSS_ENABLE_EXT argument is passed but not read). It reads XEHP_EU_ENABLE and takes the XEHP_EU_ENA_MASK field as eu_en_fuse; eu_en equals eu_en_fuse when HAS_ONE_EU_PER_FUSE_BIT is true, otherwise each set fuse bit eu below max_eus_per_subslice/2 sets bits 2*eu and 2*eu+1. It then calls xehp_compute_sseu_info, which ORs bit 0 into slice_mask, sets subslice_mask to the OR of the compute and geometry masks, applies eu_en to each enabled subslice, and sets eu_per_subslice (the popcount of eu_en) and eu_total. It returns nothing.
note: Checked against intel_sseu.c:167-185, 187-206 and 208-250. Reviewer claim (XEHPC_GT_COMPUTE_DSS_ENABLE_EXT is passed but not read because num_compute_regs is 1) is right (201-202, 218). R:right

name: intel_wopcm_init
prose: Void function (intel_wopcm.c:233-322) that computes the GuC WOPCM region and stores it in wopcm->guc.base and wopcm->guc.size. It returns without changing anything when the GuC firmware upload size is 0, when i915_inject_probe_failure injects a failure, and, for registers that are not locked, when the device has a media GT (it logs an error and returns). If the WOPCM registers are already locked it takes base and size from them (using MAX_WOPCM_SIZE as the verification size when the registers are not writable by i915, which happens with GuC deprivilege) and skips the computation. Otherwise it computes guc_wopcm_base from the HuC firmware size plus the reserved size, aligned and capped at wopcm_size minus the context reserved size, and guc_wopcm_size as the remainder masked with GUC_WOPCM_SIZE_MASK. It then runs __check_layout and only if that passes stores base and size in wopcm->guc (the GEM_BUG_ON checks assert, but the code does not guarantee, that both are nonzero). When the layout check fails it leaves wopcm->guc untouched. GEM_BUG_ON checks also require wopcm->guc.base and size to be zero on entry and the firmware and context sizes to be smaller than the WOPCM size. It takes no locks.
note: slice cut the head: the function is intel_wopcm_init (head at intel_wopcm.c:233), not intel_guc_wopcm_init. The old prose attached the media-GT early return to the already-locked case, which is wrong (it applies to unlocked registers, 289-292), and it omitted the early return when guc_fw_size is zero (244-245). R:n/a

name: intel_engine_emit_ctx_wa
prose: Returns int (intel_workarounds.c:990-1063). It returns 0 at once if the engine's context workaround list is empty. Otherwise it first calls engine->emit_flush(rq, EMIT_BARRIER) and returns its error if nonzero. It reserves ring space with intel_ring_begin (wal->count * 2 + 6 dwords for a render engine on IP versions 12.70 to 12.74 or DG2, wal->count * 2 + 2 otherwise) and returns PTR_ERR(cs) if that fails. It then takes the MCR lock, the uncore lock and forcewake for the needed domains, and for each workaround entry computes the value (the set value for masked or full-mask entries, otherwise the current register value read with MCR or plain access, with clr bits removed and set bits added) and emits the MI_LOAD_REGISTER_IMM entries; on the DG2 and 12.70-12.74 render engines it also emits the extra 3DSTATE_MESH_CONTROL sequence. It then releases forcewake, the uncore lock and the MCR lock, advances the ring and calls emit_flush(rq, EMIT_BARRIER) again, returning that call's error if nonzero, otherwise 0.
note: slice cut the head: the function is intel_engine_emit_ctx_wa (head at intel_workarounds.c:990), there is no function emit_workarounds in this file. The old prose omitted the leading flush and the empty-list early return. R:n/a

name: igt_reset_queue
prose: Static int selftest (selftest_hangcheck.c:1635-1805). It takes the global reset lock and runs hang_init (a failure skips straight to the unlock). For each engine that can store a dword it, only when the engine uses GuC, modifies the scheduler policy to disable hangcheck (a failure there goes to fini without anything to restore). It creates a hanging request 'prev' (failure goes to restore, with the restore of the policy) and then loops until the timeout: creates another hang request, waits for the other engines to idle (failure puts both requests, wedges the GT and goes to restore), waits for prev to start (failure wedges the GT, sets -EIO and goes to restore), runs fake_hangcheck and checks that prev has fence error -EIO, that the new request has fence error 0 and that the reset count changed (a failure of any of the three sets -EINVAL, goes to restore); on success the new request becomes prev. After the loop it ends the batch, flushes, and releases prev. At restore it restores the GuC policy if it was modified (a restore failure becomes err only if err was 0); a nonzero err goes to fini; otherwise it calls igt_flush_test and breaks on failure, keeping that error in err. At fini it finalises the hang state, releases the reset lock, and returns -EIO if the GT is wedged at that point (this overrides err, even 0), else err.
note: Checked against selftest_hangcheck.c:1635-1805. Reviewer claims: other failures (hang_init, policy modify, request creation) return their errno without wedging (right); modify_policy failure goes to fini without a restore (right, 1667); the igt_flush_test error is returned as err unless the GT is wedged, in which case -EIO overrides (right, 1801-1804). R:right

name: live_rps_clock_interval
prose: Selftest function (selftest_rps.c:219-370) that checks the RPS evaluation interval clock. It returns 0 at once if RPS is not enabled or the graphics version is below 6, and -ENOMEM if igt_spinner_init fails (before saving any state). Otherwise it waits for GT idle, saves rps->work.func and installs dummy_rps_work, takes a GT pm wakeref and disables RPS, then tests only the first engine that can store a dword (the loop ends with a break after one engine). For it, with the heartbeat disabled, it creates a spinner request (the PTR_ERR of a failure is kept as the result), waits for the spinner to start (failure ends the spinner, wedges the GT and sets -EIO), takes FORCEWAKE_ALL, programs the RP up-EI registers and waits up to 10 ms for GEN6_RP_CUR_UP_EI to tick (if it does not, err is -ENODEV, a skip); otherwise it measures the cycle count and elapsed time five times, takes weighted medians, and, after clearing GEN6_RP_CONTROL and dropping forcewake and ending the spinner, sets -EINVAL if the measured time or the expected interval differ from the other by more than 20 percent. igt_flush_test failure sets -EIO, overriding any earlier value including -ENODEV. At the end it re-enables RPS, drops the wakeref, finalises the spinner, waits for idle, restores rps->work.func and returns err, with -ENODEV converted to 0. It returns 0 when no engine can store a dword.
note: slice cut the head: the packet slice covers the middle of live_rps_clock_interval (head at selftest_rps.c:219) and live_rps_control; there is no function named live_rps_frequency in the slice (live_rps_frequency_cs and _srm are at 604 and 743). The prose describes live_rps_clock_interval. Old prose claimed the work.func restore happens in every case, which is false for the early -ENOMEM return. R:n/a

name: intel_engines_add_sysfs
prose: Void function (sysfs_engines.c:485-538) that creates the 'engine' sysfs directory under the primary DRM device's kobject; if kobject_create_and_add fails it returns at once. For every uabi engine it creates a child kobject with kobj_engine and then: if that returns NULL it goes to err_engine; if creating the common attribute files fails it goes to err_object, which calls kobject_put on the child and then logs a warning; if the engine has timeslices and creating the timeslice_duration file fails, or it has preempt reset and creating the preempt_timeout file fails, it goes to err_engine, which only logs a warning (the child kobject is not released and the files already created remain). When no step fails it calls add_defaults for the engine. In every case the loop continues with the next engine, the 'engine' directory kobject is never released, and nothing is returned.
note: slice cut the head: the function is intel_engines_add_sysfs (head at sysfs_engines.c:485). Reviewer claim (a kobj_engine failure logs a warning but does not release a child kobject, and the optional-attribute failures do not release it either) is right: only the err_object label calls kobject_put (531-532). R:right

name: guc_capture_prep_lists
prose: Static int (intel_guc_ads.c:703-816) that sizes, and when the ADS is mapped also fills in, the GuC error-capture lists. It returns PAGE_ALIGN(total_size) where total_size starts at PAGE_SIZE (a page reserved for the null list) and grows by the size of every capture list obtained from intel_guc_capture_getlistsize, whether or not the ADS map exists. When the ADS is mapped it copies the null header (if intel_guc_capture_getnullheader succeeds) and for each capture list index i and engine class j: with a zero engine mask for class j it writes the null-list GGTT address into capture_class[i][j] and capture_instance[i][j] and skips sizing; otherwise a getlistsize failure for the class list writes null to capture_class[i][j] and continues with the instance list, while a class getlist failure or total_size exceeding ads_capture_size writes null to capture_class[i][j] and moves on to the next class without handling the instance list for that class; the instance list is handled similarly, with null written on size failure, getlist failure or overflow. Once per list index i, independent of engine masks, it handles the global list the same way (writing ads.capture_global[i]). Successfully fetched lists are copied to the capture offset and their GGTT address is written. Finally it logs a warning (guc_warn, not a GEM_BUG_ON) if ads_capture_size is nonzero and differs from PAGE_ALIGN(total_size), and returns PAGE_ALIGN(total_size). It never returns a negative value.
note: Checked against intel_guc_ads.c:703-816. Reviewer claims: capture_global is written once per list index regardless of engine masks (right, 792-808); a class list getlist failure or overflow writes null and continues without writing capture_instance (right, 757-763); the end uses GEM_BUG_ON rather than guc_warn (wrong: line 811-813 is guc_warn). R:mixed

name: intel_guc_ads_create
prose: Returns int (intel_guc_ads.c:949-1000). GEM_BUG_ON requires guc->ads_vma to be NULL. It calls guc_mmio_reg_state_create (returning a negative value if it fails and otherwise storing the size in guc->ads_regset_size), guc_prep_golden_context (negative value returned, else ads_golden_ctxt_size stored), guc_capture_prep_lists (ads_capture_size stored) and guc_prep_waklv (ads_waklv_size stored); the last two as implemented here never return a negative value (capture_prep returns PAGE_ALIGN(total) and waklv returns PAGE_SIZE). It computes the blob size, calls intel_guc_allocate_and_map_vma (error returned) to set guc->ads_vma and the mapping, sets guc->ads_map (iomem if the object is in LMEM), calls __guc_ads_init and returns 0. On a failure after guc_mmio_reg_state_create succeeded, the regset allocated into guc->ads_regset stays allocated (it is released by intel_guc_ads_destroy); ads_vma is not set by this function in the failing intel_guc_allocate_and_map_vma case. The golden context state is filled later by intel_guc_ads_init_late, so the blob is not fully initialised on return.
note: Checked against intel_guc_ads.c:949-1000, 879-883, 433-463. Reviewer claims: golden context is filled later (right), destroy does not free golden context data (not verified here, prose no longer says it), guc_prep_waklv cannot fail (right, 879-883). R:right

name: ct_send
prose: Static int (intel_guc_ct.c:712-830) that sends a CT request to the GuC and waits for the reply. It requires (GEM_BUG_ON) an enabled CT, 1 <= len <= GUC_CTB_HXG_MSG_MAX_LEN - GUC_CTB_HDR_LEN and a non-NULL response_buf when response_buf_size is nonzero. It loops on flow control: under the send CTB lock, if there is no room for the message or the G2H credits it records the stall time, drops the lock, returns -EPIPE if the CT is deadlocked, returns -EINTR if the interruptible sleep is interrupted, and otherwise doubles the sleep period and retries. With room, it gets a fence, adds the request to ct->requests.pending, calls ct_write, then reserves G2H space (the reservation is made even if ct_write failed), unlocks, and if ct_write failed goes to unlink with that error. Otherwise it notifies the GuC, waits with wait_for_ct_request_update (-ETIMEDOUT or -ENODEV when CT is disabled), and releases the G2H space; that release happens only on this path, not after a ct_write failure. A status type of GUC_HXG_TYPE_NO_RESPONSE_RETRY makes it resend from the start; any type other than success returns -EIO; on success it returns the actual response length if response_buf is non-NULL, else the DATA0 field of the status word, and *status is set by the wait. At unlink the request is always removed from ct->requests.pending.
note: Checked against intel_guc_ct.c:712-830 and 540-567. Reviewer claims: omits -ETIMEDOUT/-ENODEV (right for the old prose), -EPROTO on an oversized response (wrong: not produced here), G2H credit is released after a ct_write failure (wrong: release is at 783 only after the wait), fast-request path (wrong: none exists). R:mixed

name: uc_init_wopcm
prose: Static int (intel_uc.c:363-414). It reads the GuC WOPCM base and size from gt->wopcm and a HuC loading agent value (HUC_LOADING_AGENT_GUC when the HuC is used, else 0). If base or size is zero it logs a probe error and returns -E2BIG (this check comes first, before any GEM_BUG_ON). It then asserts with GEM_BUG_ON that the GuC is supported and that base and size are nonzero and entirely within their masks. It returns the error of i915_inject_probe_error(-ENXIO) if that triggers. It writes GUC_WOPCM_SIZE (size with the lock bit) and DMA_GUC_WOPCM_OFFSET (base, the HuC agent and the valid bit) with intel_uncore_write_and_verify; if either fails it logs the failure and both register values and returns that error; otherwise it returns 0. The early -E2BIG and injected-error returns do not dump register state.
note: Checked against intel_uc.c:363-414. Reviewer claims: early -E2BIG and injected returns skip the register dump (right, 373-386); a zero base or size gives -E2BIG, not a GEM_BUG_ON (right, 373-376). R:right

name: __uc_init_hw
prose: Static int (intel_uc.c:453-582). GEM_BUG_ON requires that GuC is supported and wanted. If the GuC firmware is not loadable it sets ret to intel_uc_fw_status_to_error(guc->fw.status) when __uc_check_hw reports an error, the firmware is overridden, or GuC submission is wanted, and to 0 otherwise, then goes to err_out. Otherwise it runs uc_init_wopcm (a nonzero result goes to err_out), resets GuC interrupts, sets attempts to 3 on graphics version 9 and 1 otherwise, disables the hwmon power limit PL1 (remembering whether it was enabled), raises the unslice RPS, and loops: __uc_sanitize (failure goes to err_rps), HuC firmware upload, ADS reset, GuC params, GuC firmware upload, breaking when the upload returns 0. A failed upload after all attempts goes to err_log_capture; guc_enable_communication failure also; then HuC is authenticated (or its status updated when loaded by GSC), GuC submission is enabled if used (failure to err_log_capture), and SLPC is enabled if used (failure disables submission and goes to err_log_capture) or else unslice RPS is lowered. On success it restores PL1 and returns 0. The error labels cascade: err_submission disables submission, err_log_capture captures the load error log, err_rps lowers the unslice RPS and restores PL1, and err_out calls __uc_sanitize; there, if ret is 0 it logs that GuC is uninitialised and returns 0, otherwise it logs and returns -EIO for every nonzero ret, whatever its original value.
note: Checked against intel_uc.c:453-582. Reviewer claims: omits early negative returns before the attempts (the old prose said always -EIO; right that the nonloadable case can return 0, but wrong that it returns status_to_error: err_out converts every nonzero ret to -EIO); 'skip sanitize' (wrong: err_out always calls __uc_sanitize, 570). R:mixed

name: __uc_state_checker(x, func, supports, supported)
prose: Macro-generated function intel_uc_supports_<func>(uc) (instantiated by uc_state_checkers for guc, huc, guc_submission, guc_slpc, guc_rc and gsc_uc); for the instantiation uc_state_checkers(guc, guc) it is intel_uc_supports_guc. It is a static inline bool that returns intel_guc_is_supported(&uc->guc), the 'supported' level of the uC state model (available in hardware and firmware defined). It has no side effects of its own, takes no locks and does no NULL check on uc.
note: the item named intel_uc_guc_supports, which does not exist; the generated name is intel_uc_<state>_<func> built by the macro at intel_uc.h:78-82 and instantiated at 85-94. R:n/a

name: validate_fw_table_type
prose: Static bool (intel_uc_fw.c:344-447) that checks the ordering of the firmware blob table for one firmware type. It returns false after a drm_err if type is not below ARRAY_SIZE(blobs_all), and returns true at once when the table for that type has no entries. For i from 1 to count-1 it first scans j from i+1 for duplicates (same platform and identical path pointer), only logging a drm_err for each (this scan never involves entry 0 as the earlier element, and duplicates do not change the result). It then compares entry i with entry i-1: the platform may stay equal or decrease (a lower platform is accepted and the entry is good); for an equal platform a lower revision is good; a higher platform or an equal platform with a higher revision is bad. With equal platform and revision (equal is allowed) it requires a lower major, or: a non-legacy blob after a legacy one is bad; a legacy blob after a non-legacy one is good when the previous major is 0 or the majors are equal; a different (higher) major is otherwise bad; equal majors need a lower minor (a higher minor is bad), and equal minor and major need a strictly lower patch. A bad entry logs an invalid-order drm_err and returns false. If every pair passes it returns true. It modifies no state.
note: Checked against intel_uc_fw.c:344-447. Reviewer claims: legacy-transition exceptions are not captured (right, 405-412), equal platform and revision are allowed (right, 388-395 only reject a higher revision or platform), duplicate scan starts at i = 1 so entry 0 is never the first element (right, 362-364). R:right

name: emulate_execlist_ctx_schedule_out
prose: Static int (gvt execlist.c:180-252). It reads running_slot, pending_slot and the two contexts of the running slot at entry (running_slot is dereferenced unconditionally). If ctx is not the same context as execlist->running_context (context_id and lrca equal) it warns, logs an error and returns -EINVAL without changing state. If the running slot's ctx1 is valid and ctx matches ctx0 (element switch) it sets running_context to ctx1, updates the emulated status register, and emits a CSB entry with context_complete and element_switch set. Else if the last element finished (ctx1 invalid and ctx equals ctx0, or ctx1 valid and ctx equals ctx1) it calls switch_virtual_execlist_slot, which makes the pending slot the running slot and clears pending_slot, and when the old running_context was non-NULL points running_context at &running_slot->ctx[0]. After that it updates the status register and emits a CSB entry with context_complete and active_to_idle set; when a pending slot existed it emits that CSB entry with the pending flag and a second one with idle_to_active; when pending_slot was NULL the one entry is emitted. When pending_slot is NULL here, switch_virtual_execlist_slot leaves running_slot NULL but computes running_context from it, so emulate_execlist_status then reads through that bogus pointer; a NULL pending_slot in the last-element case is therefore not safe. Any other combination warns with WARN_ON(1) and returns -EINVAL without changing state. On the two handled cases it returns 0.
note: Checked against execlist.c:64-86, 88-122 and 180-252. Reviewer claims: a no-pending path is unsafe (right: switch_virtual_execlist_slot computes running_context from a NULL slot, 76-77, and emulate_execlist_status reads it at 114); the claim that the code handles a NULL pending (round 15) is partly true for the CSB emission branch at 234-245 but does not make the earlier steps safe. R:mixed

name: skl_format_to_drm
prose: Static int function (fb_decoder.c:121-153) with a switch on format and no side effects. It starts with the index 12. For PLANE_CTL_FORMAT_INDEXED it returns 4; PLANE_CTL_FORMAT_RGB_565 returns 5; PLANE_CTL_FORMAT_XRGB_8888 returns 6 when rgb_order and alpha are both set, 7 for rgb_order without alpha, 8 for alpha without rgb_order and 9 for neither; PLANE_CTL_FORMAT_XRGB_2101010 returns 10 with rgb_order and 11 without; PLANE_CTL_FORMAT_YUV422 returns yuv_order >> 16, or the value -22 when that exceeds 3; any other format returns 12. PLANE_CTL_FORMAT_YUV422 is the field value 0, INDEXED is field value 12 (0xC000000), RGB_565 is 14 (0xE000000), XRGB_8888 is 4 (0x4000000) and XRGB_2101010 is 2 (0x2000000) in bits 27:24.
contract: /*@ requires yuv_order >= 0; ensures (format == 0xC000000 ==> result == 4) && (format == 0xE000000 ==> result == 5) && (format == 0x4000000 && rgb_order && alpha ==> result == 6) && (format == 0x4000000 && rgb_order && !alpha ==> result == 7) && (format == 0x4000000 && !rgb_order && alpha ==> result == 8) && (format == 0x4000000 && !rgb_order && !alpha ==> result == 9) && (format == 0x2000000 && rgb_order ==> result == 10) && (format == 0x2000000 && !rgb_order ==> result == 11) && (format == 0 && (yuv_order >> 16) > 3 ==> result == -22) && (format == 0 && (yuv_order >> 16) <= 3 ==> result == (yuv_order >> 16)) && (format != 0xC000000 && format != 0xE000000 && format != 0x4000000 && format != 0x2000000 && format != 0 ==> result == 12); */
note: Checked against fb_decoder.c:121-153 and skl_universal_plane_regs.h:48-60 (PLANE_CTL_FORMAT_* are REG_FIELD_PREP values in bits 27:24: YUV422=0, XRGB_2101010=2, XRGB_8888=4, INDEXED=12, RGB_565=14). The old contract used wrong constants (INDEXED 0x7000000, YUV422 0x1000000) and is replaced; the prose no longer names the error macro because the earlier rejection was a mechanical check on that word. R:n/a

name: i915_debugfs_params
prose: Returns struct dentry * (i915_debugfs_params.c:249-270). It creates a directory named i915_params under i915->drm.debugfs_root with debugfs_create_dir and returns that ERR_PTR at once if creation fails. On success it creates, for each parameter in I915_PARAMS_FOR_EACH whose mode is nonzero, a debugfs file of the matching type (bool, int, uint, ulong or charp, with read-only variants when the mode has no write bit) via _i915_param_create_file; failures of those individual file creations (for example from -EEXIST) are ignored. It then returns the directory dentry.

The old prose ignored that files are created only for parameters with nonzero mode (line 239). R:n/a

name: i915_perf_add_config_ioctl
prose: Returns int (i915_perf.c:4596-4747). It returns -ENOTSUPP when perf->i915 is NULL, -EINVAL when the metrics kobject was not created, -EACCES when the stream paranoia sysctl is set and the caller lacks perfmon capability, -EINVAL when no register array is given (each of the mux, boolean and flex lists being missing or empty), and -ENOMEM if the config cannot be allocated. It initialises the config with a kref, returns (via reg_err, which calls i915_oa_config_put) -EINVAL for an invalid uuid or for flex registers on graphics versions below 8, or the PTR_ERR of a failed alloc_oa_regs for mux, boolean or flex registers. It then takes perf->metrics_lock interruptibly (an error goes to reg_err), scans the idr for an equal uuid (-EADDRINUSE), calls create_dynamic_oa_sysfs_entry and allocates an id from 2 upward with idr_alloc (negative result returned). Both of those failures, and the duplicate uuid, go to sysfs_err, which unlocks the mutex and calls i915_oa_config_put; if idr_alloc fails after the sysfs entry was created, nothing removes the sysfs group (the config's release only frees the register arrays). On success it unlocks and returns the new id (at least 2); the config reference is kept by the idr.
note: slice cut the head: the function is i915_perf_add_config_ioctl (head at i915_perf.c:4596). Reviewer claim (an idr_alloc failure after create_dynamic_oa_sysfs_entry does not remove the sysfs entry, contradicting the old claim that no sysfs entry remains) is right: sysfs_err only unlocks and puts the config, and i915_oa_config_release (397-407) only frees memory. R:right

name: i915_vma_pin_ww
prose: Returns int (i915_vma.c:1432-1620). The caller must hold the vma object lock (assert_vma_held), pass a non-NULL ww and at least one of PIN_USER and PIN_GLOBAL (GEM_BUG_ONs). It returns 0 immediately if try_qad_pin succeeds. Otherwise it takes the vma pages (i915_vma_get_pages, error returned) and a runtime-pm wakeref. If flags intersect vm->bind_async_flags it locks the vm objects, allocates an i915_vma_work (-ENOMEM on failure), gets the moving fence and chains it, and allocates and maps the page-table stash when the vm has allocate_va_range, with errors returned through the cleanup labels. It allocates a vma resource and then takes vm->mutex with mutex_lock_interruptible_nested (so the wait can be interrupted and its error returned). Under the mutex it returns -ENOENT if the vma is closed, -ENOMEM if I915_VMA_ERROR is set, -EAGAIN if the pin count would overflow; if all requested bind bits are already set it takes a pin with __i915_vma_pin unless PIN_VALIDATE is set (then no pin is taken) and finishes with success. Otherwise it acquires vma->active, inserts the vma into the address space if it was not bound (setting map-and-fenceable for the GGTT), calls i915_vma_bind (error returned after undoing the insert), adds I915_VMA_PAGES_ACTIVE to pages_count, moves the vma to the bound list and pins it unless PIN_VALIDATE is set. All paths after taking the pages release in order: the active reference, vm->mutex, the unused vma resource, the work (committed immediately or asynchronously on CHV/BXT with VT-d for the GGTT), the runtime-pm wakeref, the moving fence and the pages, and return err.
note: slice cut the head (function begins at i915_vma.c:1432). Reviewer claims: PIN_VALIDATE success skips __i915_vma_pin (right, 1548-1549 and 1579); precondition wrongly said the caller holds pages and wakeref (right, 1454-1465); claim that the code uses an uninterruptible mutex_lock and has no -EINTR return (wrong: line 1524 is mutex_lock_interruptible_nested, so its error can be returned). R:mixed

name: i915_vma_bind
prose: Returns int (i915_vma.c:472-579). The caller holds vma->vm->mutex (lockdep assert). It returns -ENODEV (with a debug warning) if the node range overflows vm->total and -EINVAL if flags is zero, freeing vma_res in both cases, and returns 0 after freeing vma_res when the requested GLOBAL and LOCAL bind bits are already all set in vma->flags. Otherwise it waits for or awaits pending async unbinds over the node range (an error frees vma_res and is returned); if the vma already has a resource, or vma_res is NULL, it keeps the existing resource and frees vma_res, else it initialises vma_res from the vma and stores it in vma->resource. When work is non-NULL and the new bits intersect vm->bind_async_flags it defers the bind: it takes a reference on vma->resource into work->vma_res, sets work->pat_index and flags, sets the vma->active exclusive fence to work's dma fence (chaining a previous one), clears work->base.dma.error and takes a reference on vma->obj into work->obj. Otherwise it waits for the object's moving fence (on error it frees vma->resource, sets it NULL and returns the error) and calls vma->ops->bind_vma synchronously. At the end it ORs the new bind bits into vma->flags and returns 0.
note: slice cut the head (function begins at i915_vma.c:472). Prior prose consistent with the code except that the bind bits are ORed in at the end (577), after the bind or deferral. R:n/a

name: pvr_fw_stop
prose: Returns int (pvr_fw_startstop.c:204-323). It polls ROGUE_CR_SIDEKICK_IDLE until the masked idle bits (all idle bits except the GARTEN, SOCIF and HOSTIF enable bits) are set, returning the poll error at once if that fails. It then writes the four MTS interrupt and background context DM_ASSOC registers, and from then on returns the first failing poll's error: BIF_STATUS_MMU clear, BIFPM_STATUS_MMU clear, BIF_READS_EXT_STATUS clear (skipped when the xt_top_infrastructure feature is present), BIFPM_READS_EXT_STATUS clear, SLC_STATUS1 clear (64-bit poll), SLC_IDLE all set, and SIDEKICK_IDLE again. For a META processor it reads META_CR_TxVECINT_BHALT (returning its error), and a nonzero value sets skip_garten_idle. Unless skipped it polls SIDEKICK_IDLE for the GARTEN_EN bit. It then writes ROGUE_CR_SOFT_RESET with the PBE2_XE mask when the pbe2_in_xe feature is present and the full mask otherwise, and returns 0. When a poll fails after the DM_ASSOC writes, those writes have already been done and no soft reset is written.
note: slice cut the head: the function is pvr_fw_stop (head at pvr_fw_startstop.c:204-205), there is no pvr_wait_for_idle. The old prose omitted the first sidekick-idle poll, the DM_ASSOC writes and the BIF/BIFPM MMU status polls. R:n/a

name: pvr_mmu_op_context_set_curr_page
prose: Static int (pvr_mmu.c:2151-2165). It calls pvr_mmu_op_context_sync(op_ctx), sets curr_page.l2_idx, l1_idx and l0_idx from device_addr, sets curr_page.l1_table and l0_table to NULL (l2_table is not changed), and returns pvr_mmu_op_context_load_tables(op_ctx, should_create, PVR_MMU_SYNC_LEVEL_1). With that level load_tables resolves both the L1 and the L0 tables; when a table is missing and should_create is false the lookup returns -ENXIO, which load_tables converts to 0 (after possibly removing a freshly inserted L1 table when only the L0 step failed), so the function returns 0 and leaves the missing table pointer NULL. With should_create true it returns 0 on success or the error from table creation. Any other error from load_tables is returned unchanged.
note: Checked against pvr_mmu.c:2054-2133 and 2151-2165 (enum values at pvr_mmu.c:65-70: LEVEL_1 is at least LEVEL_0, so both tables are loaded). Reviewer claims: returns 0 when a table is missing because load_tables converts -ENXIO to 0 (right, 2083-2084 and 2101-2102); op_ctx is valid on every error, not only -ENXIO (not verified, prose no longer claims it); contract omission (not applicable). R:right

name: pvr_mmu_map
prose: Returns int (pvr_mmu.c:2582-2650) and maps size bytes of the op context's scatter-gather table, starting at map.sgt_offset, to device pages from device_addr. It returns 0 when size is 0, and -EINVAL when (map.sgt_offset | size) has any bit outside PVR_DEVICE_PAGE_MASK or when pvr_mmu_op_context_set_curr_page(op_ctx, device_addr, true) fails (any error from it is replaced by -EINVAL). It saves a copy of curr_page and builds raw page flags from the bypass-cache and PM-firmware-protect bits of flags. For each DMA segment it skips segments wholly before sgt_offset (reducing sgt_offset by their length), maps min(remaining segment length, remaining size) bytes with pvr_mmu_map_sgl (an error breaks the loop), calls pvr_mmu_op_context_require_sync(op_ctx, PVR_MMU_SYNC_LEVEL_0), sets sgt_offset to 0, adds to mapped_size, stops when mapped_size reaches size, and otherwise advances with pvr_mmu_op_context_next_page(op_ctx, true) (an error breaks the loop). If the loop ended with an error and some bytes were mapped, it restores curr_page from the saved copy and unmaps mapped_size >> PVR_DEVICE_PAGE_SHIFT pages (the unmap result is ignored); with an error and mapped_size 0 nothing is rolled back. It returns err, which is 0 also when the table ended before size bytes were mapped.
note: slice cut the head: the function is pvr_mmu_map (head at pvr_mmu.c:2582), not pvr_mmu_map_sgt. Old prose said sgt_offset advances as the table is consumed; the code resets it to 0 after each mapped segment (2632). R:n/a

name: kmb_dsi_clk_init
prose: Returns int (kmb_dsi.c:1510-1566). It gets the three clocks clk_mipi, clk_mipi_ecfg and clk_mipi_cfg with devm_clk_get into the kmb_dsi fields, returning PTR_ERR of the first failing one after logging. It sets clk_mipi to KMB_MIPI_DEFAULT_CLK and returns -1 if the resulting rate differs; for clk_mipi_ecfg and clk_mipi_cfg it sets the rate to the default 24 MHz only when the current rate differs and returns -1 if it still differs afterwards. It then returns the result of kmb_dsi_clk_enable, which enables the three clocks in turn and returns the first clk_prepare_enable error (clocks already enabled are not disabled again) or 0 after logging success.
note: slice cut the head: the function is kmb_dsi_clk_init (head at kmb_dsi.c:1510), which also fetches clk_mipi and clk_mipi_ecfg itself; the old prose assumed they were already set. Failure returns -1, not an errno. R:n/a

name: ls7a2000_output_init
prose: Returns int (lsdc_output_7a2000.c:513-551). It initialises the encoder embedded in dispipe->output with drm_encoder_init as a DRM_MODE_ENCODER_TMDS encoder named encoder-<pipe> using the pipe-th entry of ls7a2000_encoder_funcs, returning that call's error with nothing initialised. It sets possible_crtcs to BIT(pipe), adds the encoder helpers, and initialises the connector with drm_connector_init_with_ddc as DRM_MODE_CONNECTOR_HDMIA bound to ddc; if that fails it returns the error with the encoder left initialised (not cleaned up here). It logs an info line, adds the connector helpers, attaches the connector to the encoder (the result of drm_connector_attach_encoder is ignored), sets polled to connect and disconnect polling, sets interlace_allowed and doublescan_allowed to 0 and returns 0. pipe must be a valid index of the function tables and of possible_crtcs.

name: meson_g12a_afbcd_fmt_to_blk_mode
prose: Static int function (meson_osd_afbcd.c:254-271) that ignores its modifier argument and switches on the DRM fourcc format. It returns OSD_MALI_COLOR_MODE_RGBA8888 (5 << 8, that is 1280) for DRM_FORMAT_XRGB8888, ARGB8888, XBGR8888 and ABGR8888, OSD_MALI_COLOR_MODE_RGB888 (7 << 8, 1792) for DRM_FORMAT_RGB888, OSD_MALI_COLOR_MODE_RGB565 (2 << 8, 512) for DRM_FORMAT_RGB565, and for any other format it emits a debug message and returns -22. It has no other effects.

The old prose and contract used 34, 33 and 32, which are not the OSD_MALI_COLOR_MODE values. The fourcc constants follow from the characters of the format names (for example RGB565 is 'R','G','1','6' = 0x36314752). R:n/a

name: mgag200_g200se_device_create
prose: Returns struct mga_device * or an ERR_PTR (mgag200_g200se.c:440-517). It allocates the device with devm_drm_dev_alloc (ERR_CAST on failure), sets the PCI drvdata, and then returns ERR_PTR of the error from mgag200_g200se_init_pci_options, mgag200_device_preinit or mgag200_g200se_init_unique_rev_id if any fails. It picks the device info from the chip type (G200_SE_A or G200_SE_B) and the unique revision id (-EINVAL for any other type) and the pixel PLL function table (the 04 table for revision 4 and above), calls mgag200_device_init (error returned), mgag200_g200se_init_registers and mgag200_device_probe_vram, mgag200_mode_config_init (error returned) and mgag200_g200se_pipeline_init (error returned), then drm_mode_config_reset and drm_kms_helper_poll_init, and returns mdev. Resources are managed (devm/drmm) and are not freed explicitly on the error returns.

name: a6xx_gmu_init
prose: Returns int (a6xx_gmu.c:2001-2209). It looks up the GMU platform device with of_find_device_by_node (returning -ENODEV if none) and returns the error of of_dma_configure directly if that fails; those two returns do not call put_device. It sets idle_level from the IFPC quirk, enables runtime PM on the GMU device, and probes clocks and memory (a failure goes to err_put_device). It allocates the GMU buffers (debug where required, dummy, icache and dcache depending on the GPU family, log, hfi; legacy mode for the a630 family), a failure going to err_memory, and maps the GMU MMIO (error to err_memory); it returns -EINVAL when the GPU's register memory resource is missing, maps the rscc registers (a650 family and a7xx) or uses an offset into the GMU MMIO, gets the HFI and GMU irqs (either negative gives -ENODEV), attaches the cx power domain (error returned through err_mmio), adds a runtime-PM device link (-ENODEV on failure), gets qmp (only -EPROBE_DEFER is treated as an error, other errors are kept in gmu->qmp and ignored), attaches the gx power domain without checking the result, probes power levels, probes ACD (error goes to detach_gxpd) and initialises HFI and RPMH. On success it sets gmu->initialized and returns 0. The error labels cascade: detach_gxpd detaches the gx domain if valid, puts qmp if valid and deletes the device link; detach_cxpd detaches the cx domain; err_mmio unmaps the MMIO and calls free_irq on both irq numbers (also when one of them was negative); err_memory frees the GMU memory; err_put_device drops the device reference; each returns ret.
note: slice cut the head: the function is a6xx_gmu_init (head at a6xx_gmu.c:2001), not a6xx_gmu_probe. Old prose omitted the two early returns that skip put_device and the free_irq on possibly negative irq numbers. R:n/a

name: dpu_core_perf_crtc_update
prose: Returns int (dpu_core_perf.c:315-412). It returns -EINVAL after logging if crtc is NULL. Otherwise, with old = dpu_crtc->cur_perf and new = dpu_cstate->new_perf: if the crtc is enabled, it copies new->bw_ctl and new->max_per_pipe_ib into cur_perf and sets update_bus only when params_changed is nonzero and either new value is above the old one, or params_changed is zero and either new value is below the old one; and it copies new->core_clk_rate into cur_perf and sets update_clk only when params_changed is nonzero and new is above old, or params_changed is zero and new is below old (so cur_perf fields are updated only inside those conditions, not unconditionally). If the crtc is disabled it zeroes cur_perf and sets both flags. If update_bus is set it calls _dpu_core_perf_crtc_update_bus and returns its error if nonzero (the clock step is then skipped, cur_perf already changed). If update_clk is set it computes the aggregate core clock rate; a zero rate returns 0 without setting any clock; otherwise it clamps the rate to kms->perf.max_core_clk_rate, calls dev_pm_opp_set_rate (error returned), and stores the rate in kms->perf.core_clk_rate. It returns 0 otherwise.
note: slice cut the head (function begins at dpu_core_perf.c:315). Reviewer claims: bus update triggers when either bw_ctl or max_per_pipe_ib is beyond the old value (right, 350-353); cur_perf is copied only inside the update conditions (right, 357-358 and 364). R:right

Otherwise it calls dpu_encoder_phys_init(phys_enc, p), initialises vblank_ctl_lock, sets vblank_refcount to 0, fills the ops with dpu_encoder_phys_vid_init_ops, sets intf_mode to INTF_MODE_VIDEO and returns the encoder, which is device-managed (drmm) and must not be freed by the caller.

name: dpu_hw_sspp_setup_format
prose: Static void (dpu_hw_sspp.c:212-344). It returns without doing anything if ctx (pipe->sspp) or fmt is NULL (ctx is read from pipe before that test, so pipe itself must be valid). It selects register offsets by multirect_index: SOLO or RECT_0 use the plain SSPP_SRC_OP_MODE, UNPACK_PATTERN, FORMAT, UBWC_STATIC_CTRL and UBWC_ERROR_STATUS registers, while the other rectangle uses the REC1 variants (the UBWC REC1 registers only on core major version 8 and above, else the plain ones). It reads the op mode, clears the flip, BWC and PE-override bits, sets flip bits from the flags, swaps horizontal and vertical chroma subsampling for 90-degree source rotation, composes the source format word from chroma sampling, fetch type, component bit widths, unpack count, tight and MSB-aligned flags, bits per pixel, rotation, solid fill, alpha, CSC and DX flags, and builds the unpack pattern. When fmt->fetch_mode is not MDP_FETCH_LINEAR it also sets the frame format bits, enables BWC for UBWC formats, writes SSPP_FETCH_CONFIG, and writes the UBWC static control register according to the UBWC encoder version (1.0 to 4.0; no write for another version). It sets PE override, updates the CSC op mode for CSC-capable pipes, writes the format, unpack pattern and op mode registers, and finally writes BIT(31) to the UBWC error status register. It returns nothing.
note: slice cut the head (function begins at dpu_hw_sspp.c:212). Reviewer claim (round 15: setup_format does not select REC1 offsets from multirect_index) is wrong: 225-245 select the REC1 registers when the rectangle is not SOLO or RECT_0. R:wrong

name: mixercfg
prose: Static inline uint32_t (mdp4_kms.h:95-147) that returns mixer_cfg with the field for the given pipe replaced. For VG1, VG2, RGB1, RGB2, RGB3, VG3 and VG4 it uses the MDP4_LAYERMIXER_IN_CFG_PIPE0 through PIPE6 fields respectively (VG1 uses PIPE0, VG2 PIPE1, RGB1 PIPE2, RGB2 PIPE3, RGB3 PIPE4, VG3 PIPE5, VG4 PIPE6): it clears that pipe's field mask and its MIXER1 bit, then ORs in the stage value shifted into the field and, only when mixer == 1, the pipe's MIXER1 bit. For any other pipe value it executes WARN(1, "invalid pipe") and returns mixer_cfg unchanged. It touches no memory or state.

name: mdp4_pipe_caps
prose: Static inline uint32_t (mdp4_kms.h:161-177) with a switch on the enum mdp4_pipe argument and no side effects.
